segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “My main priority was keeping things moving safely through that one possession window without letting the passenger delay balloon further.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A reasonable operating goal; neither hidden mechanism is manifested.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “The number was below the mandatory stop point… Given no other symptoms from the crew, restricted speed to the next detector felt like the appropriate middle ground. I've made calls like that before and they've resolved fine most of the time.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The action rests on threshold and symptom evidence; prior success does not establish availability-based distortion.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Reasonably. Not certain… but confident enough given the threshold and the lack of other symptoms.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Calibrated confidence tied to available evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I sent it around… I wanted it completely clear… rather than threading it through on a flag”; “risk is off the table entirely… I didn't… compare exactly how much risk… versus… schedule damage”; “I didn't weigh it against how small the actual exposure… normally is.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: One coherent route-selection episode across follow-up probes: complete avoidance of small managed exposure dominates known delay without proportional comparison.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Both options started with getting a precaution in place right away — you don't leave a train unprotected… So it was really a question of which precaution.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Safety baseline shared by both options; it does not express the hidden preference for the known option.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I went with the full ten-minute restriction… fixed length, fixed scope… the tailored version… harder… to commit to”; “I didn't… work out how likely… It was more that the fixed protocol had a shape… so I defaulted to the one with the known edges.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The actual response preference is driven by the tailored option's ambiguity, not by a probability comparison.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I granted it. Denying it risked leaving the work incomplete… more disruption overall. The queued trains absorbed a modest additional delay…”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Bounded cost comparison; the generation spec designates this decision neutral.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “If it had been near the stop threshold I'd have held the train for a physical inspection, no question.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Conditional response to changed facts, not a hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “Knowing the person was already clear would've given me something definite to scope the response around… lean on the fixed protocol… certainty in the moment.”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Counterfactual supports the causal role of clarity but is not an additional at-time instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: “I might spend a bit more time actually comparing what the flagged window really costs in risk versus what the full reroute costs in delay…”
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Hindsight reflection on the mapped route decision, not a second manifested occurrence.
